title: QGIS plugins: Esri Tile Cache Converter and S-JTSK Official Transformation
description:
Problem. Two gaps in QGIS for Slovak spatial data: (1) national maps distributed as Esri Compact V1 .tpk (e.g. national forest maps) cannot be opened; (2) the official ÚGKK transformation between S-JTSK [JTSK], S-JTSK [JTSK03] and ETRS89 / WGS 84 is not applied reliably.

State as of 23 November 2026 (QGIS 3.44.12, PROJ 9.8.1, GDAL 3.13.1, Windows): GDAL does not read Compact V1 (and the open-source tpkutils reads it only in Web Mercator); QGIS transforms ETRS89 → EPSG:5514 with the Czech parameters "S-JTSK to ETRS89 (1)", up to 4.2 m off the official ÚGKK chain in Slovakia (mean 1.9 m; confirmed in QGIS on 12 test points), and installing the official GKÚ grid alone does not change that.

Solution. Esri Tile Cache Converter converts Esri tile caches (incl. Compact V1) to GeoPackage / MBTiles without re-encoding. S-JTSK Official Transformation transforms vector layers by the official ÚGKK chain (independently of the PROJ installation; equal to PROJ with the official grid to below 0.1 mm) and, on request, makes it QGIS's preferred transformation, so QGIS's own reprojection follows it too. Checked against the binding RTS service of ÚGKK on 56 points: agrees to 6 mm (a constant 5.3 mm in the Helmert step, the grid step equal), while QGIS's default is up to 4.1 m off RTS.

Aim. Correct, reproducible work with Slovak national data in open software — for forestry, cadastre and field surveys — with an open methodology.

  • No binaries; the libraries are bundled as plain Python (MIT), the GKÚ grid as data (© GKÚ Bratislava, CC BY 4.0).
  • Requirements: QGIS 3.34 or newer. The tile converter uses numpy and Pillow shipped with QGIS for fast overviews (without Pillow it falls back to GDAL); LERC elevation caches need the optional Python package lerc.
  • Open methodology: METHODOLOGY.md in each library repository; how AI was used: AI_DISCLOSURE.md there.
